sonnet.problem: This True statement re-asks the fact card 2 just asked and revealed (David asks God for mercy). It is only a rewording of the previous choice card.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the exact word in the line ('proved right'). The baker has seen no earlier wording and cannot reason out 'right' against 'patient' or 'gentle'. The question also repeats the story card before it.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The story card says David looks back 'all the way to the very start of his life.' That gives away the answer to card 11, which asks whether David was free of sin until later in life.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the exact word 'return.' No earlier card lets the baker reason to it, and 'sing' and 'speak' fit 'sinners will ___ to God' just as well. This is guessing wording, not meaning.
sonnet.rule: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The joke 'now I talk so much my OVENS need a break' does not click. Ovens do not listen to talking, so the comparison does not match the action of going from silence to speaking.
sonnet.rule: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

sonnet.problem: The statement bundles two claims, that God delights in sacrifice and that David will therefore bring one. A baker can't mark it cleanly as one claim.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'If not burnt offerings,' which rules out the two wrong answers, since a spotless lamb and a golden offering are both physical offerings. The right answer is also the only one that isn't an object, so it stands out.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either. ... All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.
